questions.topic: Recall Stage vs Precision Stage: The Ranking Funnel
questions.question: What is the primary obligation of a recall stage?
options: Produce the final ordering that the user or answer model consumes
Admit the relevant documents into a set later stages can afford
Assign calibrated scores that every later stage can compare directly
Collapse near-duplicate passages so each source contributes once

questions.topic: Recall Stage vs Precision Stage: The Ranking Funnel
questions.question: Why is an early false negative especially harmful?
options: Later stages cannot rank a document that never reached them at all
It forces the reranker to score more pairs than its budget allows
It puts downstream scores onto a scale that cannot be compared
It raises candidate recall but leaves the final order unchanged

questions.topic: Recall Stage vs Precision Stage: The Ranking Funnel
questions.question: Four of five relevant documents enter the candidate set. What is candidate recall?

questions.topic: Recall Stage vs Precision Stage: The Ranking Funnel
questions.question: Why should unauthorized candidates be filtered before reranking where possible?
options: Filtering after fusion is impossible once the ranks have been merged
The reranker needs tenant labels as one of its scoring features
Unauthorized documents distort the calibration of the fused scores
Sending that text to the scorer already crosses a security boundary

questions.topic: Recall Stage vs Precision Stage: The Ranking Funnel
questions.question: A relevant document was retrieved but disappeared after source-level deduplication. Which stage owns the defect?
options: The dense retriever, whose approximate index missed a true neighbor
The deduplication transition, whose source-collapse rule removed it
The reranker, which scored the surviving passage below the cutoff
The ACL filter, which removed the document at the serving boundary

questions.topic: Recall Stage vs Precision Stage: The Ranking Funnel
questions.question: The reranker is unavailable. What is the strongest degraded-mode design?
options: Serve the fused order, filtered and evaluated as its own mode
Serve the lexical list alone, since fusion needs a scorer to be useful
Serve the ranking cached from the last successful run of that query
Fail the request outright so that quality never degrades silently

questions.question: What is a candidate budget?
options: The number of tokens a reranker may allocate to one document
The share of the latency budget assigned to candidate generation
The maximum number of documents the corpus index may hold
The target or maximum number of items handed from one stage to the next

questions.question: What usually happens when pairwise rerank depth doubles?
options: Pair-scoring work stays flat because batching absorbs the extra pairs
Candidate recall falls because the deeper candidates are noisier
Pair-scoring work grows roughly in proportion to the added depth
Token processing halves as the batches become larger and more uniform

questions.question: BM25 and dense search each return 100 items with 60 overlapping. How many unique candidates exist?
Why can post-filtering a vector top 50 break the planned rerank depth?
options: The filter rewrites each candidate's rank, so the fused order is lost
Only a handful of the 50 may be eligible, so the reranker sees fewer
Vector engines cannot evaluate metadata predicates after a search
Eligibility is independent per candidate, so exactly 50p items remain

questions.question: Candidate success rises from 0.968 at depth 100 to 0.973 at depth 200, while p95 latency nearly doubles. What should decide the choice?
options: Whether the deeper setting raises the offline metric by any amount at all
Whether the retriever can return 200 candidates in one round trip
Whether the sweep ran on the same hardware the fleet now uses
Whether the extra 0.005 of success is worth the latency it spends

questions.question: Under overload, which policy is safest?
options: Queue every request without limit so that no query is ever refused
Fetch each candidate's full body first so the scorer never waits
Admit within bounded queues and fall back to an evaluated depth
Raise rerank depth so fewer requests need a second retrieval round
